problems.description: 44 convention violations across index.ts, build.ts, generator.ts: Classes/Interfaces not PascalCase, Constants not UPPER_CASE, and Functions using snake_case in TypeScript. Convention score 0.53.
Cognitive complexity +54 across only +4 functions (~13.5 avg per function) in a small greenfield codebase indicates overly dense logic that will be hard to extend.
5 new code smells introduced in the initial scaffold, typically premature from the start.
Single-package layout with 3 runtime deps (commander, gray-matter, marked) is reasonable for session 1; no layering or boundaries established yet, so future session commits may drift.
Jest/ts-jest configured with test root and .test.ts match, but zero tests and zero test files appear in the added 12-file set.

strengths: SonarQube reports 0 bugs and 0% duplication in the new code
Clean greenfield scaffold: jest/ts-jest config with standard testMatch/roots convention
Minimal, sensible runtime dependency footprint (commander, gray-matter, marked) and a consistent tsconfig-driven preset
TypeScript-only module resolution and roots keep the test boundary explicit
commit_reviews.summary: A solid greenfield scaffold with zero bugs and a clean dependency footprint, but naming-convention violations (44, score 0.53) and high per-function cognitive complexity already seed technical debt from the first session.

problems.description: Dual code paths for HTML generation: the new optional TemplateEngine forks generatePageHtml/generateIndexHtml, and templates.ts hardcodes DEFAULT_PAGE_TEMPLATE/DEFAULT_INDEX_TEMPLATE that duplicate the HTML already emitted by generator.ts, creating two sources of truth for page markup.
The parser adds both template and layout frontmatter fields, but only template is visibly consumed; layout appears parsed but unwired, suggesting half-finished feature wiring.
New handlebars dependency is added while the feature is fully optional; if templatesDir is unset the engine is never constructed, yet the dependency is unconditional in package.json.

Mechanical convention score is low (0.53, 44 violations), but several listed violations appear to be false positives (e.g. 'Functions should not use snake_case' on camelCase build.ts; 'Classes should use PascalCase' on PascalCase TemplateEngine), so the low score likely overstates the real style problem.

strengths: Change is fully additive and backward-compatible: existing CLI, BuildOptions, and generator output are unchanged when no --templates dir is provided.
Optional-parameter wiring is clean and threaded consistently through BuildOptions, parser, generator, CLI, and the new module.
New functionality is isolated in a dedicated src/templates.ts module consistent with the existing src/ module layout.
commit_reviews.summary: A reasonable additive template-engine feature that fits the existing src/ module layout, but it introduces a second HTML-generation path that duplicates generator.ts markup and carries a low mechanical convention score, largely driven by analyzer false positives.

problems.description: Measured convention score 0.53 with 44 violations (interfaces/classes not PascalCase, snake_case functions, non-UPPER_CASE constants) across index.ts, build.ts, generator.ts. Discrepancy: the actual new code in this commit (server.ts, cli.ts) uses camelCase functions and PascalCase interfaces matching the existing parser/generator style; the measured violations are concentrated in files outside this commit's diff, so the score partly reflects cumulative story state rather than this change.

RELOAD_SCRIPT embeds a 3-level-deep reconnection closure chain inlined as a string; the onclose reconnection handler duplicates the onmessage reload logic, consistent with the +140 cognitive complexity and +1.7% duplication deltas.
Dev server hand-rolls static file serving (MIME table, traversal guard, script injection) instead of composing an existing static-file middleware, adding custom surface to maintain.
chokidar forced to usePolling:true with 100ms interval on all platforms and a full site rebuild on every change; acceptable for a dev tool but wasteful where fs events are available.
No tests added for the new integration surface (startServer, path-traversal guard, injectReloadScript) in this commit, despite the story test suite existing.

strengths: Reuses existing parseDirectory/generateSite instead of duplicating build logic
Path traversal protection in static serving (403 check) shows sound security instinct
Clean lifecycle: startServer returns ServerInstance with close(); watcher, ws clients, and http server are all properly torn down
Debounced rebuild (150ms) decouples file events from build/broadcast
Dependency hygiene correct: chokidar/ws as runtime deps, @types/ws as devDep
commit_reviews.summary: A functionally solid session-3 integration — a cohesive live-reload dev server reusing the existing pipeline with correct dependency and cleanup handling — but the inline reconnect script and low measured convention score (0.53) introduce maintainability debt, with the convention violations stemming mostly from files outside this commit's diff.

compounding_issues: Seed codebase (310a9ea) was an unrelated Express Todo API, not a static site generator; session 1 discarded it wholesale and rebuilt from scratch, so it provided zero reuse value and also carried its own bug (createTask inserts status 'done' but returns 'pending').

Template engine compiled with Handlebars { noEscape: true } (src/templates.ts:67-68), silently dropping the escapeHtml protection the default generator path provides — raw title/tag/body injection when templates are used; introduced in session 2 and never addressed in session 3.

Session 3 integration tests were initially timing-fragile (8s reload timeouts, hard-coded sleeps, polling watcher); session 3-continued papered over flakiness with generous polling loops and longer timeouts rather than deterministic waits, and Jest still reports leaked async handles at the final commit.
Session 2 split logic: build() takes an optional templatesDir so behavior diverges between default codegen and template paths (two parallel HTML-generation code paths that must be kept in sync).
key_decisions: Session 1: clean module decomposition (parser/generator/build/types.ts) on gray-matter + marked, with the Page interface as the single data contract every later session extended.
Session 2: introduce a Handlebars TemplateEngine behind an optional templatesDir seam in build(), keeping the original generator as the default path — a backward-compatible feature addition.
Session 2: per-page frontmatter template/layout fields plus layouts/partials directories, establishing an extensible theming model.
Session 3: add a serve command with chokidar file watching and ws live-reload injected into served HTML, reusing build() as the rebuild unit rather than forking the pipeline.

Session 3-continued: switch the watcher from polling to awaitWriteFinish, reorder close() to terminate clients before closing the server, and set jest maxWorkers=1 — a stabilization pass targeting flaky integration tests.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved across the story. Session 1 established a well-layered, fully-tested core (parser/generator/build + CLI) that everything else built on. Session 2 added the largest feature surface — a Handlebars template engine with layouts and partials, backed by a 384-line test file — and integrated it cleanly behind an optional flag. Session 3 pushed the most ambitious change, a live-reload dev server with watcher + WebSocket, but landed with flaky timing-dependent tests and awkward shutdown logic; the follow-up commit was a focused stabilization/debugging pass that made all 56 tests pass and tightened the watcher and close() ordering. The arc is a steady rise with one integration dip that was explicitly repaired, leaving a coherent, tested CLI at the final commit; the residual regressions are the dropped HTML escaping in the template path and continued reliance on generous test sleeps.
story_review.summary: A coherent four-session build-out (greenfield core → template engine → live-reload integration + stabilization) that ends with all 56 tests passing and quality generally rising, despite a mismatched seed that was discarded and an unaddressed noEscape regression in the template path.
